antagonist_line: Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end.
gm_thesis: Every act offers at least one guaranteed and one earned hint that the danger is manufactured and the forest is not the enemy.
surface_plot: Survive or resolve the Bramble Union ambush.
Deliver the Keystone Asset to Hush.
Help the Custodian install the wardstone.
Defend Open Vale until the ward renews.

tag_legend.REFLAVOR: Retell the existing beat through the manufactured-threat lens.
tag_legend.SEED: Plant the truth without explaining it.
tag_legend.GUARANTEED: GM narrates it; every table sees it.
tag_legend.EARNED: Requires a roll, mercy, curiosity, or follow-up.

pacing_schedule.label: Onboarding + Prologue
pacing_schedule.context: pregens, safety, connections, Contract overview, Job briefing, forest threshold
pacing_schedule.lever: Keep the Contract to plain setup, let the Job carry questions, then move to the blocked road.

pacing_schedule.label: Act 1: Logistics Incident
pacing_schedule.lever: Skip the staged-bramble earned seed; move to ambush sooner.

pacing_schedule.label: Act 2: Bramble ambush
pacing_schedule.lever: Abstract the fight via a Group Action roll; keep one captured reclaimer for the interrogation seed.

pacing_schedule.label: Act 3: Hush
pacing_schedule.context: social beat, Co-op, local leads, optional break
pacing_schedule.lever: Trim village wandering to the invoice plus one elder line; point to the Custodian.

pacing_schedule.label: Act 4: Hanging Office
pacing_schedule.context: Custodian, Keystone reveal, new objective, short rest
pacing_schedule.lever: Compress the reveal; bank the Short Rest into travel narration.

pacing_schedule.label: Act 5: Open Vale defense
pacing_schedule.lever: Lower the countdown start to 6; cap wraith reinforcements.

pacing_schedule.label: Epilogue
pacing_schedule.context: win, congratulatory-report cliffhanger, Relay Spire hook
pacing_schedule.lever: Deliver the report prop and the hook even if you skip the slip.

Prologue.text: Grail-branded bounty board: "STRIXWOLF: APEX FOREST HAZARD. Sightings up 300%. Bounty payable in Marks."
Couriers or a clerk trade fearful route gossip: the Preserve "takes one a week now."
A player asking what they know receives the corporate line: strixwolves are vicious pack predators.

Act One.text: The Strixwolf Mother is feeding pups and guarding them; she reacts to tone, not bloodlust.
Act One.roll: Presence to calm; Instinct to read boundaries

Act One.text: The driver died from a cut throat; the strixwolf did not kill him.
Near the cart is a pre-written Grail "Hazard Confirmed: Strixwolf Attack" tag.
Helping the pups or sparing the mother earns Hope now and can create a later warning boon.

Act Two.text: The reclaimers target the cargo and manifest, not purses, and avoid killing when possible.
Their gear includes salvaged, repainted Grail/Kazrak kit: ex-workers, not feral bandits.
Act Two.roll: Knowledge Medium 15 to name the issue

Act Two.text: "That stone belongs in the ground." "You do not know what you are carrying."
A spared/captured reclaimer says monster attacks spiked when protection contracts went on sale.
Act Two.roll: Presence Medium 15; requires mercy or capture

Act Three.text: A Grail "Protection Coverage" invoice hangs on the Clover Co-op wall, overdue and steep.
Firstmoss and the Sunless Farms show the forest feeding Hush rather than hunting it.
An elder says, "The wood was never this bad. The trouble came with the waymarkers."
A ledger shows protection costs and hazard sightings climbing together.

Act Four.text: The sealed package is the capital's ward Keystone; the city is unwarded while it is away.
"The wood never needed managing. It needed leaving alone."
"Your capital's safety is older than your contracts. It is the very thing they teach you to fear."
The Keystone's magic is pre-corporate forest-ward work, the same school companies call primitive.
The Custodian glances at obsolete Soulspire inspection seals on her counterweight boulder.

Act Five.text: Soul-Audit Wraiths bear audit glyphs and say, "Unlicensed soul-resonance detected. Submit for audit."
A defeated wraith leaves a Soulspire compliance tag or coil-credit token instead of natural remains.
Wraiths ignore forest creatures and home only on ritual soul-magic.
A player can read the markings and name Soulspire without the GM naming it first.
Optional flag: Legacy Skeletons carry scraps of old corporate credentials.

Epilogue.text: The ritual completes, Hush is safe, and the Custodian thanks them. The win is real.
A Grail/Kazrak incident report thanks them for "neutralizing forest hazards" and supporting continued Protection Coverage.
If pushed, the Custodian admits the "hazards" were not always here, then looks away.
A nearby Relay Spire beacon burns weakly, pointing to the larger thread.
